resolved_source_issues.issue: The lecture assigns rather than completes the first-order frequency-shift estimate.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter derives delta nu over nu approximately gh over c squared from the stated light-travel time and acquired velocity.

resolved_source_issues.issue: A Newtonian argument alone does not establish exact free-fall cancellation at every order.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter states the leading calculation and preserves the lecture's requirement for special-relativistic Doppler factors in the exact result.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Informal scalar notation can look as if values at two different points are being equated.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter equates the x and y coordinate representations evaluated at the same geometric point.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The vector-product construction could be read as defining every rank-two tensor as one decomposable product.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter uses the product only to derive the transformation pattern and explicitly removes the stronger claim.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Pointwise flattening and exact flattening on a neighborhood can be conflated.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter distinguishes normal coordinates at one point, flat finite regions, and the cone's local-global obstruction.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The angular coordinate names vary during the live sphere discussion.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter defines phi as polar angle and theta as azimuth before writing the standard unit-sphere metric.

uncertain_sources.note: The numerical weak-shift formula is a standard completion of the exercise explicitly assigned in the lecture.
The video cuts to closing material before a clean completed sphere formula remains on screen; the geometric diagram and spoken construction determine the typeset result.
